problem:
Found on 2026-11-13 by driving a clean PyPI 2.1.0 install through the quickstart (three Haiku agents on a two-file project). The planner, builder and reviewer all did good work, but the task never reached a reviewed merge:

- "Start reviewer on this" on the **completed** card starts an ordinary work turn (`/agent/trigger` with `task_id`, `hub/ui/src/api/tasks.ts:1074-1085`), not a review (`review_task_id`). The task stays `completed`; the reviewer may not decide evidence or approve, and correctly does neither.
- Asking the reviewer in its conversation ends the same way: it needs an evidence grant.
- Dragging the card to Under review is refused with "dispatch a different agent's review turn (POST /agent/trigger with review_task_id)".
- Only "Land it" merges — in one click, with no confirmation, while all four evidence rows are still awaiting.

A build (flow) already staffs a reviewer for completed work (`scheduler.resolve_reviewer`, rungs 1–3), but the quickstart's path — approve, then start tasks by hand — has no build, so nothing routes the finished task to review. The product's headline promise ("a different agent reviews it, and approving it merges it") is not what a first-time user experiences.

Operator decisions, 2026-11-13: (1) "Start <agent> on this" on finished work is a real review; (2) when nobody is named to review, the Hub picks someone other than the author and says so, rather than refusing; (3) "Land it" asks for confirmation and says it skips review.

requirements.rationale: The label promised a review and delivered a work turn; the review turn is what lets a reviewer decide the evidence and approve.
requirements.statement: On a task in `completed`, the card's start menu MUST offer each open agent other than the task's author as "Review with <agent>", and choosing one MUST start that agent's review turn on the task, moving it to `under_review` with that agent as its reviewer; the author MUST NOT be offered.

requirements.rationale: The operator chose "pick someone and say so" over refusing approval: a newcomer who skipped naming a checker still gets a review.
requirements.statement: When a task that belongs to no running build reaches `completed` and its project checks pass, the Hub MUST start a review turn by the task's declared checker if one resolves, otherwise by an open agent other than the author chosen as a build would choose one; when none can be chosen, the task MUST show why (e.g. "no agent other than the author to review this") instead of waiting silently.

requirements.rationale: Choosing silently would read as if somebody had named that reviewer.
requirements.statement: A review the Hub staffed without a declared checker MUST say so on the task's story, naming the reviewer and that nobody was declared.

requirements.rationale: One click merged unreviewed work during the drive; the operator keeps the power, but knowingly.
requirements.statement: "Land it" MUST ask for confirmation before merging, stating that it merges without a review and, when any of the task's evidence is still awaiting, how many pieces are unreviewed; cancelling MUST change nothing.

requirements.rationale: The quickstart is the first thing a new user follows; it failed on 2026-11-13.
requirements.statement: The quickstart's review-and-merge step MUST describe the path this change provides, and following it on a fresh install MUST end with the task approved by a reviewing agent and merged.

summary: A task started by hand from the board, as the quickstart teaches, is reviewed by a different agent and merged on that agent's approval — without the operator having to discover "Land it". The card's start menu offers a review on finished work, a finished task with no build behind it gets a reviewer by itself, and "Land it" says plainly that it skips review.
